Our licensed technicians repair tub diverter valves, clear dense hair traps, and install alcove, drop-in, and freestanding tubs with precision.

emergency.heading: Bathtub actively leaking through ceiling or overflowing? Call now.

steps.title: Stop water flow to the bathtub immediately
steps.text: Turn off the shower and tub faucet valves firmly. If the valve fails to shut off, close the bathroom fixture stop or main water shutoff.

steps.title: Do not drain standing tub water if lower ceiling is leaking
steps.text: If water is dripping through ceiling drywall on the floor below, leave the tub stopper closed until a plumber inspects the waste shoe.

steps.title: Protect lower levels with buckets
steps.text: Place plastic bins or towels beneath ceiling water drips on lower floors to minimize drywall and wood flooring damage.

steps.title: Call our licensed bathtub plumbing team
steps.text: Tell us whether you need emergency leak repair or are planning a planned bathtub upgrade or replacement.

symptoms.title: Water dripping into ceiling drywall below second-floor tub
symptoms.text: A cracked waste-and-overflow shoe or failed rubber drain gasket leaking water into lower-level drywall whenever the bathtub drains.

symptoms.title: Tub drain draining sluggishly with standing bathwater
symptoms.text: Dense hair clusters, soap scum, and hard-water mineral crust restricting the tub P-trap and linkage assembly inside the overflow pipe.

symptoms.title: Water leaking from tub spout when showerhead is running
symptoms.text: A worn gate diverter mechanism inside the tub spout failing to seal completely, wasting hot water and reducing showerhead spray pressure.

symptoms.title: Bathtub floor flexing, squeaking, or cracking
symptoms.text: A fiberglass or acrylic bathtub installed without proper supportive mortar base bedding shifting under body weight until the floor cracks.

symptoms.title: Outdated, chipped, or stained builder-grade tub
symptoms.text: Aging porcelain-on-steel or discolored acrylic tubs from the 1980s or 1990s that homeowners want replaced with modern soaking designs.

symptoms.title: Water pooling around exterior tub caulking seam
symptoms.text: Deteriorated perimeter silicone caulk allowing shower splash water to penetrate behind tile boards and subfloor framing.

phoenixAngle.heading: Why Phoenix Hard Water & Dry Air Impact Bathtub Plumbing
paragraphs: Bathtub plumbing fixtures in the Phoenix Valley are heavily impacted by extreme municipal tap water mineral hardness. In our hot desert climate, dissolved calcium carbonate and magnesium deposit thick white mineral crusts inside tub spout diverter gates, waste-and-overflow linkages, and brass drain clicker mechanisms. Over time, these minerals seize moving diverter parts, causing shower water to dribble uselessly from tub spouts.

Furthermore, Phoenix's extremely low indoor humidity dries out builder-grade acrylic tub caulking and rubber waste gaskets, leading to unseen leaks that soak subfloor framing when tubs are filled. Our licensed plumbing technicians install heavy-duty brass valves, solid PVC waste shoes, and 100% silicone mildew-resistant seals designed to endure intense Valley conditions.

facts.text: Hard water mineral scale in Phoenix binds tub diverter gates and calcifies waste-and-overflow drain linkages.

costFactors.intro: Bathtub repair and replacement pricing depends on job scope (drain shoe repair vs. complete tub replacement), tub style, and wall access.

factors.title: Drain shoe repair vs. full tub replacement
factors.text: Replacing a leaking waste-and-overflow shoe takes less labor than removing an alcove tub and tiling surrounding walls.

factors.title: Freestanding vs. alcove tub design
factors.text: Freestanding tubs utilize specialized drop-in drain kits, while alcove models require framing tie-ins and apron leveling.

factors.title: Tile and drywall access requirements
factors.text: Accessing plumbing through a rear bedroom closet opening saves tile demolition compared to opening tile-surrounded tub decks.

factors.title: Mortar base bedding installation
factors.text: Setting acrylic tub basins in structural wet mortar beds prevents future floor flexing, squeaking, and basin cracking.

faqs.q: Why is water dripping through the ceiling whenever someone takes a bath?
faqs.a: Water dripping into the room below is almost always caused by a failed tub waste-and-overflow assembly or a degraded rubber drain gasket seal. When the tub is filled with heavy water weight or drained, water seeps through the unsealed connection and drips directly through ceiling drywall.

faqs.q: Why does water still come out of my tub spout while the showerhead is running?
faqs.a: The lift-gate diverter inside your tub spout is designed to block water and force it upward to the showerhead. In Phoenix, hard-water calcium scale coats the internal plastic or brass diverter gate, preventing it from sealing completely and allowing hot water to escape out the tub spout.

faqs.q: Can a plumber replace my bathtub without ripping out all the bathroom tile?
faqs.a: For standard alcove bathtubs, removing the tub generally requires cutting away the bottom row of wall tile where the tub flange sits. However, if upgrading to a freestanding soaking tub in a spacious bathroom, existing wall tile can often remain completely untouched.

faqs.q: Why does the bottom of my acrylic bathtub flex and squeak when I stand in it?
faqs.a: Fiberglass and acrylic bathtubs require a solid wet mortar or plaster bedding beneath the basin floor during original installation. If the builder skipped this step, the flexible plastic basin bends under human body weight, causing squeaking noises and eventually causing structural floor cracks.

faqs.q: How long does it take to replace a residential bathtub in Phoenix?
faqs.a: A standard bathtub plumbing replacement—removing the old tub, upgrading drain lines, setting the new tub in mortar, and connecting the waste assembly—typically takes one to two working days, depending on whether tile surround repair or wall finishes are part of the scope.

faqs.q: Do I need a city permit to replace a bathtub in Phoenix?
faqs.a: Rules differ by city and by the specific work being done. Replacing an existing bathtub in the exact same location with matching plumbing rough-ins often differs from moving walls or relocating drain lines. Your licensed plumbing contractor will clarify all applicable permit and inspection requirements.
